SCULPT CLEAN — OFFLINE A-SPADE PORT

Upstream project: https://github.com/andryr/spade-declipping
Author: Andry Rafaralahy
Copyright (c) 2023 Andry Rafaralahy
License: MIT; the complete text is in LICENSE in this directory.
Pinned commit: d9285bc5d6874670c462773f4c0dba55c6d7f66b

Unmodified upstream reference files are included in this directory:
tight_aspade.m, declip.m, hard_thresh.m, redundant_dft.m,
redundant_idft.m and LICENSE. Their Git blob hashes are recorded in
../PROVENANCE.json and were checked against the stored bytes.

Source/OfflineRepair.h adapts the A-SPADE loop from tight_aspade.m,
the hard coefficient threshold from hard_thresh.m, the windowed framing
and normalization from declip.m, and the unitary FFT normalization from
redundant_dft.m / redundant_idft.m.

Changes in the Sculpt port (2026):
- Native C++17 implementation, without MATLAB or the LTFAT runtime.
- A unitary radix-2 DFT / inverse DFT is used as the tight frame;
  this port does not use a redundant analysis dictionary.
- Reusable operation-local buffers and a precomputed FFT table.
- Original conservative near-rail/flat-plateau detection, with separate
  positive and negative rail estimates per channel.
- Adjustable iteration count, clipping threshold, amount and peak bound.
- Conjugate-pair threshold consistency for real-valued synthesis.
- Original free-region projection for manual sparse audio inpainting.
- Context/selection validation, finite-value checks and progress reporting.
- Transactional cancellation and commit: cancellation does not leave a
  partially modified input file.
- Unclipped samples remain byte-for-byte unchanged by the de-clip stage;
  manual repair changes only the selected sample range.

The implementation and tests do not establish equivalence with iZotope RX,
nor do they reproduce the complete set of SPADE survey experiments.

Algorithmic references:
S. Kitic, N. Bertin and R. Gribonval, "Sparsity and cosparsity for audio
declipping: a flexible non-convex approach," LVA/ICA, 2015.
P. Zaviska, O. Mokry and P. Rajmic, "S-SPADE Done Right: Detailed Study
of the Sparse Audio Declipper Algorithms," arXiv:1809.09847v4, 2020.
https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.09847
